notes: T758 — why did directive-ID uniqueness leak a third D041? ANSWER: the write path is `managent tell` → cmdTell → appendDirective, and it is a path NO uniqueness check covers. cmdTell (src/managent/main.zig:10050) minted the id as `D{sys_directive_next}` where `sys_directive_next` is loaded from `_sys.directive_next` in tasks.json — a DIFFERENT file from the ledger (docs/infra/managent/directives.jsonl, DIRECTIVES_FILE at main.zig:7435). T545 made the counter RACE-safe (lock→read→modify→write) but never made it AUTHORITATIVE: a direct store write / restore of tasks.json rolls the counter back while the ledger keeps its max id. Recorded rollbacks: a5fc80a (T567 scrub, 55→21), 4973f0d (T568, 22→21), 416033f (T716 census, 34→21); live store now has directive_next=21 vs ledger max D079. The third D041 (line 421, target T721, from fable/holistic via Orcha, ts 2026-08-23T01:57:43Z, read:false — the appendDirective field shape, no read_by/read_at) was written by cmdTell/appendDirective minting from a counter that had been rolled back to 41. ENUMERATED WRITERS of directives.jsonl (denominator = 2, both found by grep of DIRECTIVES_FILE + `createFile`): (1) appendDirective (main.zig:7564) — the append path, sole caller cmdTell; (2) cmdInbox's ack path (main.zig:10212, rewrite at createFile main.zig:10369) — re-serialises every line in place to set read:true, mints nothing. tools/directive_policy.py only READS the ledger; src/absorb.zig does not touch it; the regression scripts write only their own scratch ledger. FIX (test-first, red→green): (a) cmdTell now mints from max(counter, ledger_max + 1) — main.zig:10050 uses @max(sys_directive_next, maxDirectiveId(...)+1), with maxDirectiveId (main.zig:7540) reading the ledger and directiveIdNumber (main.zig:7529) parsing D<digits> suffixes; (b) appendDirective gained a uniqueness backstop (main.zig:7564+, parse each existing line, return error.DirectiveIdCollision on a duplicate) so the no-two-lines-share-an-id invariant holds at the single append chokepoint whatever the minting logic did. RED recorded against the pre-fix binary (git stash of main.zig, rebuild): arm 1 (counter==an id already in the ledger) → DUP:D041, D041 x2; arm 2 (counter below ledger max) → minted D001 not D042. GREEN against the fixed binary: tools/regression-directive-id-uniqueness.sh all three arms pass (stale-counter-equal-existing-id mints fresh; stale-counter-below-max self-heals past max; ack rewrite preserves every id once). Wired into `zig build test` (build.zig, directive_id_uniqueness_regression step) — confirmed the step runs and passes under the gate (log: `=== regression-directive-id-uniqueness: ALL CONTROLS PASSED ===`). SIDE-EFFECT HANDLED: the T758 mint change exposed a STALE expectation in tools/regression-managent-concurrency.sh arm 2 (asserted directive_next==2 after a tell on a ledger arm 1 had left 10 directives in; pre-fix that 'passed' only because the old mint silently wrote a duplicate D001). Corrected arm 2 to clear the scratch ledger before its reset (its purpose is the flock-hold lost-update property, not the mint base); the T545 concurrency regression now passes all five arms against the fixed binary. PRE-EXISTING failures observed during the gate run, UNRELATED to T758 (no code touched in their paths): regression-directive-kill.sh arm 8d (T616 session-limit misclassified verified=fail vs unreached), regression-window-resilience (T628/T677), regression-fleet-keeper (T496).
